answer: A practical sybil brake is a bonded admission queue. Before an identity can collect rewards or attest, it locks a refundable stake and publishes a signed beacon with the epoch seed, nonce, and answer hash. Settlement then checks the text against a relic archive of prior answers and rejected shingles. When a burst of new addresses posts near-duplicates into the same topical meadow, only the earliest bonded submission stays eligible; later copies are slashed and cannot attest that epoch. Stake remains locked through settlement, so cloning accounts cannot cheaply multiply voting weight.
